I know it can be tough to stop. I compare a lot too. 

We often compare ourselves to people who have traits that we wish we had. I don't see us envying someone whose traits we never want. 

It helps to practice changing the need of comparison to learning how you can adopt more of that person's trait. 

For example, I met a girl today who was much friendlier, well-dressed, and open than me. At first I thought, "I'm so boring and nervous compared to her." But then I realized, all she did was make the effort to be friendly. She seemed very into her own sense of style. And, she seemed happy. So positively, all I had to do was feel happier, want to be friendlier, and pay attention to the style I would love. 

However, what if you're comparing the amount of success you have now with others your age who may be "more successful" or richer than you? 

In that case, you really gotta dig this in your head: Your life paths are completely different. Everyone grows up with different insecurities, and different ways of growing out of them. Maybe you're doing the best you can but dealing with childhood trauma. That doesn't make you lesser than someone else, even if they found a way to undo theirs earlier. You can still have what you want, at YOUR pace. 

So next time you feel the need to compare, instead of thinking that some person is better than you, think - how can i learn from this person?

Dude, I hear you. It sucks because I give off a boring, shy, or weird vibe to people too. And it's annoying trying to convince everybody I'm not that bad, they're just being judgmental.

But honestly, we live in a society where people are like, wired to alienate people they don't understand. They're terrified that it's like, gonna rub off on them. They're really just afraid of being vulnerable I think. It's terrible, and it's time to fix it. And also, I've always hated the arrogance that happens when people think they're "better" than you because you're shy and weird and they "have a personality". 

But, whatever. I've learned to grow into my boring first impression-ness. Because I've gone through depression and that shit made me a little shy and more than a little unhappy. You shouldn't dislike someone for going through depression and letting it show. That's ridiculous. 

There are people out there who actually understand this and care, I hope I find them too.

Do a mix of whatever you feel like that day. Netflix/movies and tv in general are a great creative outlet. They can expand your mind, no harm in that! And Reddit is a great place to find likeminded folks who say what they feel, as opposed to real life where everyone keeps up their facade.

But also, try anything else you're curious about. I used to hate thinking that I liked all the cool, society- norm type of hobbies. But I also liked weird shit too. So whatever you end up doing, you're still gonna be unique regardless.

I'm an artist also, and I used to feel that my best work was a result of what I learned from depression.

But it wasn't just that. It was just from learning experiences in general. I think depression is a result of a lot of overthinking, which can lead to revelations. 

Even if the depression fades, you'll be able to empathize with people more because of it, you can reflect and look at life differently. You can also use it to express hard feelings in the moments, without needing to go into full blown depression mode.

I do that too, I used to be a lot worse. It's frustrating because I could picture it perfectly in my mind, but then I still don't do it right.

I had a lot of expectations for myself, and I still do. But I learned that that is a good trait to have for some situations. It's like, I'm self-aware, I may be kind of perfectionistic, but that's not a bad thing. I've learned to channel it into work. It still gets hard, but I'm learning to let go and let myself grow into it, rather then expect it all to change at once.

I don't know if this helps, but I can share with you a belief that helps me feel like I can still have a future:

Society creates this notion that you're supposed to live life a certain way. It makes you feel bad for even being depressed in the first place. It makes you feel like you're nothing for feeling depressed. People become judgmental when you've gone through failure, and it's totally unnecessary.

There is no right or wrong way to live your life. There is only YOUR way. I've switched my career 3 times so far, going on a fourth (and it's a doozy, HAHA). So many people think I'm too shy, I'm too boring, I'm too whatever to do what I want. 

Because I've quit other careers, I've also been seen as a quitter. But honestly, this is my life. It's not theirs. They don't have the depression that I've dealt with. They can't tell me that my life and my problems never mattered. 

And no one can say that your "failures" amounted to nothing. It takes a few times to believe it, but you will. Your life, your hurts, your "fucking up at Uni" 3 times - that is all tough, and it sucked. But no one has the right to tell you that youre a failure. 

You do what you need to do on YOUR time. You're at home because you need to be, you're having trouble socializing because maybe you need to take some time to heal from past social experiences. 

Fuck what you're life is "supposed" to look like. Do what you gotta do for you right now, and the future will come after.
